data.title: Space
data.tagline: Use empty space to show which things belong together
data.description: Related items should sit close together, while separate groups need more room between them. That empty room is spacing. A product usually defines a small spacing scale so pages follow a visible rhythm instead of using a new value each time.

use: Keep a label close to the field it describes
Separate one content group from the next
Give text and controls enough room to breathe
Build a reusable spacing scale for the whole product
avoid: Choose a different spacing value for every element
Use empty space to hide a weak information structure
Leave related items farther apart than unrelated groups
Add large gaps that force unnecessary scrolling

lessonPractice.title: In a profile form, each label is far from its own field but crowded against the next label. Which adjustment best communicates grouping?

options.label: Use exactly the same gap between every label, field, and group
options.feedback: Equal distances do not reveal which label belongs to which field, so the grouping remains ambiguous.

options.label: Reduce label-to-field spacing and increase spacing between field groups
options.feedback: A smaller gap signals association, while a larger gap marks a new group. Reusable spacing steps keep this relationship consistent.

options.label: Insert spaces and blank lines into the text until the current view looks right
options.feedback: Manual whitespace breaks when copy or fonts change. Layout rules should express spacing relationships.

data.agentPrompt: Adjust the profile form spacing so labels stay close to their fields and separate field groups use a larger reusable gap. Do not position content with spaces or blank lines. Verify grouping with long labels and at mobile width.
